a:r.a:t: REVISION NOTE: The old deck showed death statistics (p.6–7) and rehab access (p.9), but the real problem only appeared after the solution, on p.18. This slide states Ausculta’s actual gap: the exam is weak (37% sensitivity) and leaves no record, and it names the user (an RHU nurse or midwife). “Diagnosis is one visit. Recovery is forty.” had no source, so it was removed. The journal screenshot on old p.19 is now a citation in the footer. SCRIPT (0:20): The problem isn’t the health workers; it’s the method. On its own, the stethoscope misses 63 of every 100 lung conditions. It saves no sound, so no visit can be compared and no doctor can review it later. And recovery support barely exists: only 2.7% of people with COPD worldwide could get pulmonary rehab.
